rows.title: Software Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
rows.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the role:
With best-in-class autonomy and real-time cloud connectivity, drones are becoming critical infrastructure for solving real-world problems faster, safer, and more efficiently. Our customers, from public safety agencies to industrial and enterprise operators, rely on Skydio Cloud to plan missions, manage fleets, and make sense of the data their drones collect.
As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll help build the systems and features that power autonomous drone operations at scale. You’ll work across the stack, from backend services in Python and Go to frontend experiences in TypeScript and React, and you’ll own meaningful pieces of work from idea to shipped feature. Our team works on a wide range of challenges and we go where we’re needed:

 - Building customer-facing features in the Skydio Cloud web app, such as fleet health monitoring, media asset management, and device management

 - Designing and extending the APIs and data models that connect drones, docks, and the data they produce

 - Visualizing rich spatial data through maps and 3D views

 - Improving the reliability, performance, and observability of the systems behind it all

The variety of work means there are plenty of opportunities to learn and have a meaningful impact on how Skydio builds and delivers software. The ideal candidate is a junior, senior, or master’s student with hands-on experience developing complex web applications, but above all, we’re looking for a highly curious and resourceful candidate, capable of using tools and AI at their disposal to accelerate their understanding and productivity.
Project Examples:

 - Building a system that allows product teams to manage feature flags and roll out functionality to customers, including both the backend service and the admin interface.

 - Developing a new view in the web app that surfaces real-time fleet status and health for customers operating many drones and docks.

 - Building tools for browsing, filtering, and managing photo and video assets captured by drones.

 - Developing a test framework that allows developers to simulate vehicle states and test how the application behaves end to end.

 - Profiling backend and frontend performance and optimizing how data is loaded and displayed to users.

What makes you a good fit:

 - Solid computer science fundamentals.

 - Meaningful project and/or internship experience building complex web applications, ideally touching both frontend and backend.

 - Proficiency with Python, Golang, and/or JavaScript/TypeScript.

 - Experience with a modern frontend framework such as React.

 - Familiarity with RESTful or GraphQL APIs and relational databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL).

 - Enjoys taking a feature from concept through design, implementation, testing, and deployment.

Bonus points for:

 - Experience with cloud services (e.g. AWS, GCP, Azure) or containerized deployments (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes).

 - Experience with geospatial data, mapping, or visualization tools such as Mapbox, Cesium, PostGIS, or ThreeJS.

 - Experience integrating frontend applications with real-time data systems.

 

Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $58 for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience.

*For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location.

rows.description:
ABOUT NOOKS.AI http://Nooks.ai:

Nooks is an applied AI lab building revenue agents that power some of the fastest growing companies in the world. We build AI agents that operate across the full revenue lifecycle, from account strategy to prospect research and outreach. Building 0→1 has never been easier, but selling at the speed of the market remains the last frontier for AI. Our mission is to 10x every seller by automating the busywork so they can focus on what humans do best: closing deals.

Today, over 2000 customers power their revenue growth using Nooks, including Notion, HubSpot, Cursor, and Rippling. We've raised over 70M USD from top VCs like Kleiner Perkins, and we have more than tripled ARR each year for 3 years running. 




BUILD THE FUTURE OF AI-POWERED WORK.

At Nooks, we're building AI agents that automate the most important function for every company: revenue generation.

Our customers use Nooks to build agents that research accounts, run outreach, and work deals across the whole revenue lifecycle. They trust us to deliver the infrastructure across text, voice, computer use, and data to power their inbound, outbound, and deal execution. Every day, thousands of users rely on Nooks to do the work that used to take entire teams of people.

Because every company in the world has a revenue function, we're still incredibly early in our product lifecycle, which means engineers have an outsized impact. You'll ship production code on your first day, own projects from idea to production, talk directly with our customers, and help define what building and maintaining AI-native enterprise software looks like.

If you want to spend your early career helping companies solve their hardest problems, building products people genuinely love, and working alongside a team that is high-intensity, high-trust, low-ego, and playing to win, we'd love to meet you. Early in your career, the environment you choose matters more than almost anything else.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a new graduate engineer, you'll work across the stack and collaborate closely with product, design, and customers to build features that ship quickly and make a measurable impact.

You'll:

 - Design, build, and ship using React, TypeScript, Node.js, and Python.

 - Own projects from initial idea through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

 - Work directly with customers to understand their problems and turn feedback into product improvements.

 - Build product that powers agent-building, real-time collaboration, enterprise-scale workflows and automations, and human-agent interaction.

 - Improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of our platform.

 - Low-latency voice AI on live calls and live coaching

 - Work across the entire agent development lifecycle, from agent-building to simulations and evals to monitoring and feedback loops.

 - Improve the efficiency and cost of our agents, through better agent design and context engineering.

 - Write clean, maintainable code and contribute thoughtful feedback and review.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're much more interested in how you think and the outcomes you are ambitious enough to drive than whether you've used every technology in our stack.

You'll likely be a great fit if you:

 - Are completing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field.

 - Have built software and agents through internships, research, open source, startups, or personal projects.

 - Have gotten stuck on something hard and found a way to push through.

 - Care whether what you build matters to the people using it.

 - Love learning new technologies and figuring out how to use them to solve problems for people. Experience with React, TypeScript, Node.js, or Python is a plus, but not required.

 - Thrive in fast-moving environments where engineers take ownership and make product decisions.

 - Able to collaborate with teammates, be truth-seeking and low-ego, and communicate technical ideas clearly.

 - Can work from our San Francisco or Seattle offices.


HOW WE WORK

 - Ownership. You’ll ship to production on your first day. From there, you'll progressively take ownership of larger features while pairing closely with experienced engineers, learning about our customer problems, product, and infrastructure. By the end of your first few months, you'll be expected to own both customer and product outcomes end-to-end. You’ll talk directly to customers, watch how they use what you built, and decide what to change.

 - Customer Empathy. You’ll talk directly to customers, watch how they use what you built, and decide what to change.

 - Intensity. We move fast because we’re intense about outcomes and building trust with our customers. If our product is not the best, we sprint to fix it.

 - Agency. The ideas that can change the trajectory of a product or company can come from anywhere. 

 - AI-native. We build agents, and we invest in their ability to give us the most leverage possible. You will be in an environment where you are constantly learning how to leverage agents to increase your craft and velocity.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Compensation for this role includes competitive base salary, meaningful equity, and comprehensive benefits. Our benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, hybrid work, and unlimited paid time off. Benefits may vary based on location and are subject to change.

The base salary range for this role is $200,000, in addition to equity and benefits.

BENEFITS & PERKS *

YOUR MISSION

Software is the central nervous system for True Anomaly's engineering and product thesis. Software bridges the gap between military objectives, theoretical astrodynamics and the human and autonomous control of spacecraft and ground systems in time and space. True Anomaly is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineer to contribute across our React/TypeScript frontend and Elixir backend, building features end-to-end across our spacecraft mission control and distributed ground control systems.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Assist in building features that span the full stack, from web-based frontend interfaces (2D and 3D) to distributed backend services powering satellite command and control, mission planning, and data processing

- Write testable and maintainable code across both React/TypeScript and Elixir codebases following industry best practices

- Work on smaller, well-defined tasks under the guidance of senior engineers, gaining depth across the stack

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including space operators, designers, frontend specialists, backend specialists, and astrodynamics algorithm engineers

- Participate in design and code reviews to continually improve code quality across both frontend and backend systems

QUALIFICATIONS

- 0-2 years of software development experience

- Understanding of HTML/CSS and modern TypeScript/JavaScript

- Familiarity with modern React (Hooks, Context API, functional component patterns)

- Functional programming experience in Elixir and/or Erlang

- Exposure to testing frameworks across the stack (e.g., Jest, Vitest, React Testing Library, ExUnit)

- Basic understanding of gRPC, RESTful, WebSocket, or GraphQL-based services

- Familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL

- Comfort with Git and Agile tools and processes

- Comfort both contributing to existing systems and building from scratch

- U.S. Citizen and eligible for DoD Secret or TS/SCI clearance

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

- Bachelor’s degree in computer science or similar discipline

- Some experience building, shipping, and maintaining real production software

- Experience using React to build complex yet performant data-rich/dense applications

- Understanding of OTP concepts including GenServers, supervision trees, and the Actor model

- Experience with distributed systems concepts and fault-tolerant architecture

- Experience in Three.js, React Three Fiber, or other web-based 3D libraries and frameworks

- Familiarity with component libraries, design systems, Storybook, and CSS-in-JS

- Experience with monitoring and tracing in distributed systems

- Experience in UI/UX design and support tools like Figma

- Strong collaboration and communication skills that let you thrive in a culture that values respectful, professional, and constructive conflict

COMPENSATION

- Base Salary:

- Denver: $75,000

- Long Beach: $80,000

Your actual level and base salary will be  determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Responsibilities

rows.title: Internal Acceleration, Research Engineer (Kernels)
rows.description:
JOB SUMMARY

Our Internal Acceleration team’s mandate is to build agents to accelerate the production of frontier tokens.

You’ll work directly with our founders and embed with our kernels team to build new agentic harnesses and operating systems to transform the way hardware is built in an AI native world. You’ll work on harnesses, tool use, context, and memory, execution environments, and evals that let agents conduct long-running engineering work that is useful.

This role is for engineers who thrive on ambiguity, have real product sense, and want to own problems end to end. It’s a whiteboard for future founders. The problems we solve are time-sensitive and business-critical. This role will not be a 9-5, and the ideal candidate is excited about that.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have at least 1-5+ years of experience building and shipping software end to end, ideally at a fast-moving startup

 - Have built agents for complex, multi-step tasks that people depend on, beyond calling an API: tool design, long-context management, evals, and failure analysis.

 - Are a strong software engineer who has built reliable systems others depend on, such as distributed systems, experiment infrastructure, or developer tooling.

 - Use coding agents heavily, read their transcripts closely, and change the system when an agent is confidently wrong.

 - Have high agency in unfamiliar domains. You find the real problem and drive it forward.

 - Have product sense, design taste, and extreme attention to detail


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Embed with our kernels team to find the highest-leverage bottlenecks, and own each one from first idea to a tool engineers rely on every day.

 - Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP.

 - Build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, EDA flows, compilers, profilers, and real hardware.

 - Ship full-stack internal products from zero to one: the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure that define how Etched builds.

 - Measure what works. Design evals and track adoption so we double down on the tools that matter and kill the ones that don’t.

 - Take on special projects directly with the founders, surfacing problems across the company and doing whatever it takes to hit critical milestones.


STRONG CANDIDATES MAY ALSO HAVE

 - Exposure to chip development, kernels, hardware, or manufacturing.

 - Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps experience

 - Fine-tuning, RAG over proprietary technical data, or multi-agent orchestration

 - Startup experience, especially through hypergrowth


BENEFITS

 - Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
   
   - $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits

 - Housing subsidy of $2,500 per month for those living within walking distance of the office

 - Relocation support for those moving to San Jose (Santana Row)

 - Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification


BASE COMPENSATION RANGE

 - $150K – $400K+

 - Plus Significant Equity


HOW WE’RE DIFFERENT

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.


ABOUT ETCHED

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

rows.title: SDET Intern
rows.description:
WHAT MAKES US EPIC?

At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

QUALITY ASSURANCE

What We Do

The Quality Assurance team owns the testing process, risk management, and quality evaluation of all products and functions across Epic. Our team works closely with developers and production to ensure the best possible user experience for our community and customers.

SDET INTERN

What You'll Do

Epic Games Art Ops team is looking for a smart, creative Software Development Engineer in Test Intern. Art Ops is the team that builds the tools, pipelines, and Al workflows our artists use for game development and emerging tech every day. This role focuses on testing those internal tools and frameworks; you'll embed with our team of engineers and technical artists to help design and build everything from Cl pipelines, test plans, and integration tests for our web apps to checks that tell us how well our Al tools are performing.

In this role, you will

- Write test plans for new tools and features, then turn them into automated tests

- Help design and build the test framework our team will use going forward, with our engineers reviewing your code

- Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for our web apps and pipeline tools

- Test how Al tools and workflows perform when new models are released, and help build ways to measure their performance

- Support weekly release testing and turn repeated manual checks into automated tests

- Investigate test failures, determine why a test broke, and share results with the team

- Use Al-assisted tools to help run, write, and triage tests, and review what they produce

What we're looking for

- Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science or a related field

- Comfortable writing code in at least one modern OOP language such as Python, C++, or C#, through coursework or personal projects

- Basic understanding of software testing, such as unit and integration testing

- Familiarity with a version control system

- Interest in Al for content and code generation

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to confidently collaborate with senior team members and take feedback on technical topics and features

- Willingness to dive into new things and drive them forward

- A personal project repository or demo portfolio is required

- Some experience with test frameworks like Jest, Pytest, or Playwright, Cl systems like GitHub Actions, or Al evaluation tools like LangChain or DeepEval is desired

- Exposure to art tools such as Unreal Engine, Maya, or Houdini, or interest in how artists work is highly desired

This internship has a flexible start date in 2027. Recruitment will be ongoing until teams find an ideal match. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the posting location for the duration of the internship. For more information about Epic’s Early Career Program, visit epicgames.com/earlycareers . This is going to be Epic!

Epic Games​ ​is a leading interactive entertainment company. For over 30 years we've been making award-winning games and engine technology that empowers others to make visually stunning games and 3D content that bring environments to life like never before. Epic's award-winning Unreal Engine technology not only provides game developers the ability to build high-fidelity, interactive experiences for PC, console, mobile, and VR, it is also a tool being embraced by content creators across a variety of industries such as media and entertainment, automotive, and architectural design. As we continue to build our Engine technology and develop remarkable games, we strive to build teams of world-class talent.

Like what you hear? Come be a part of something Epic!

Epic Games deeply values diverse teams and an inclusive work culture, and we are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. Learn more about our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy here .

We will not pay any fees to any unauthorized third party. Further details on these matters can be found here .

rows.title: Software Engineer, Backend New Graduate
rows.description:
SOFTWARE ENGINEER — NEW GRADUATE




ABOUT US

At Prophet Security, we’re not just building a platform that automates complex security tasks—we’re building a company where every team member directly impacts customer success. You’ll work closely with our customers, understand their needs, and see firsthand how your work makes a difference.

Prophet Security’s founding team brings more than 30 years of cybersecurity experience from leading companies, including Abnormal Security, Expel, Mandiant, McAfee, Oracle, Red Canary, Red Hat, Riverbed, and Symantec. We are focused on disrupting the $400 billion security labor market by building the future of automated security operations.

We’re seeking recent and upcoming graduates to join our engineering team. If you’re excited to build impactful products, grow alongside experienced engineers, and take meaningful ownership at a fast-growing startup, we encourage you to apply.


WHAT OUR PLATFORM DOES

Our platform analyzes security alerts, develops and executes investigation plans, and produces detailed findings and actionable recommendations. Security analysts review these investigations and provide context and feedback, which are continuously incorporated into future automation.


THE IMPACT YOU’LL HAVE

As a New Graduate Software Engineer, you’ll help build and evolve the core backend systems that power Prophet’s platform. Working alongside experienced engineers and experts in product, machine learning, and cybersecurity, you’ll contribute to services that ingest, process, and reason over large volumes of security data.

Example projects may include:

 - Integrations at scale: Building extensible frameworks for integrations with third-party security systems, including SIEMs, EDR/XDR platforms, identity providers, and cloud and SaaS logs.

 - Proof-of-Value pipelines: Developing performant, reliable backends that enable fast customer onboarding and compelling proof-of-value experiences, from data ingestion to actionable insights.

 - Security data platforms: Designing storage, indexing, and access patterns for highly dimensional, time-oriented security data used in real-time analysis and historical investigations.

 - AI-powered security workflows: Developing and evaluating agents and automation that help security teams investigate threats more quickly and effectively.

You’ll write production code, participate in technical design, collaborate across teams, and take ownership of projects from development through deployment. You’ll receive guidance and mentorship while gaining the independence to solve meaningful technical and customer problems.

Our technology stack: AI-powered agents, data synthesis and correlation, security-tool integrations, Python, Go, React, and TypeScript.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Recently completed or currently completing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Experience with one or more relevant programming languages, such as Python or Go, through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects.

 - Understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts, including data structures, algorithms, testing, and system design.

 - Demonstrated experience building software through academic, internship, research, open-source, or personal projects.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills.

 - Ability to collaborate effectively and learn in a fast-moving environment.

 - Passion for building high-quality products and solving customer problems.

Experience with backend services, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, or machine learning is helpful but not required.


OUR CULTURE

Our employees are our greatest asset. We provide competitive benefits, meaningful equity participation, and a fun, inspiring environment in which to learn, create, and collaborate.

 - Customer Centricity: We place customers at the center of our decisions and strive to exceed their expectations.

 - Practicality over Perfection: We favor effective solutions, thoughtful tradeoffs, and agile decision-making.

 - Strive for Excellence: We hold ourselves to high standards and continuously improve.

 - Transparent Communication: We encourage open, honest dialogue and build trust through collaboration.

 - Unwavering Resilience: We persist through challenges and remain focused on achieving our goals.

 - Have Fun: We balance hard work with creativity, enjoyment, and a positive team environment.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Prophet Security is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse, global talent pool and the collaboration that results from an inclusive team. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Our hiring decisions are based exclusively on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

rows.title: Robotic Systems Integration Engineer - Entry Level (SLA & SLS)
rows.note: Entry Level in the title; text still asks for previous experience with electro-mechanical systems
rows.description:
About Formlabs:

A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

Your Impact:

Formlabs already has a substantial business selling 3D printers and resins to dental customers, who use our products for a wide spectrum of applications, from convenient in-office production of splints to sophisticated lab-based orthodontics.

This role involves supporting all parts of the product development cycle from early R+D to continuing engineering for shipped products. In addition, you’ll collaborate closely with design teams to overcome cross-disciplinary problems and ensure that we ship quality products. If you’re eager to collaborate with other Systems Integration Engineers to support the full range of Formlabs products, we want you as a  Robotic Systems Integration Engineer .

The Job:

- Bring together the firmware and hardware of the subsystems into one system, bring prototypes through integration hell, and ensure that they work optimally as per requirements and deliver physical prototypes

- Partner with system architect to create and document visual descriptions of systems and subsystems and their inputs and outputs.

- Establish the interfaces between the sub-systems, define/refine control algorithms or even design sub-systems that are electro-mechanical in nature.

- Take ownership of managing sub-system/system level requirements and track changes.

- Design test plans to validate the requirements of subsystems/entire system, execute the tests and analyze the results.

- Resolve systems issues to improve their performance or recommend corrective actions to the functional group.

You:

- Have previous experience designing complex electro-mechanical systems.

- Knowledge of motion control, sensors and control algorithms.

- Experience managing system and subsystem requirements.

- Well versed in hardware debugging and passionate about understanding why things work (or don’t)

- Scripting experience with Python (preferred), Labview, Matlab, etc.

Bonus Skills :

- Familiarity with low-level embedded firmware (C++ prefer)

- Experience in data analysis and reporting

- Experience with consumer electronics

Our Perks & Benefits:

- Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer

- An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs

- Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job

- 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement

- Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)

- Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it

- Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)

- Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

- Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso

- Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons

- One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities

You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
Compensation:

Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

The annual base pay range for this role is:
$110,000 — $140,000 USD

rows.title: Vehicle Software Engineer - Summer Internship 2027
rows.description:
Advanced Reentry Technologies

Who We Are:

Inversion is an aerospace and defense company pioneering advanced reentry technology to enable next-generation capabilities from space. By combining high-performance materials, precision aerodynamics, and mission-driven autonomy, Inversion is transforming reentry into an operational capability for an entirely new class of missions.

The company’s highly maneuverable reentry spacecraft, Arc, is designed for rapid global cargo delivery, hypersonic testing, and other national security missions that require precise, controlled flight through the atmosphere. Arc creates an entirely new transportation domain, unlocking unprecedented speed and global reach.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, Inversion designs, manufactures, and integrates its spacecraft under one roof, enabling the company to move rapidly from concept to flight. The company is backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, with customers across the U.S. government and commercial space industry.

Position Overview:

As a Vehicle Software Engineering Intern at Inversion, you will help develop the software systems that enable our next-generation reentry vehicles to operate reliably, both in space and on the ground. You will work alongside experienced flight and ground software engineers to build, test, and deploy software that directly supports spacecraft development, qualification, and mission operations.

Unlike traditional internships focused on smaller assignments, you will take ownership of a meaningful engineering project, driving it from initial requirements and design through implementation, testing, and delivery. Your work could involve flight software, ground systems, hardware integration, or automated testing infrastructure, depending on team priorities and your interests.

This is a hands-on opportunity for students passionate about software engineering, embedded systems, robotics, or aerospace to build production-quality software that will continue to be used long after their internship ends.

Key Responsibilities

- Own a well-scoped software engineering project from requirements definition and technical design through implementation, validation, and deployment.

- Design, develop, and test software that supports spacecraft flight systems, ground operations, or engineering test infrastructure.

- Develop and integrate software with physical hardware, simulation environments, or existing flight and ground software systems.

- Write automated tests and contribute to software verification using unit testing, software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), or processor-in-the-loop (PIL) environments.

- Collaborate with flight software, avionics, simulation, and other engineering teams to solve challenging technical problems.

- Participate in software design reviews, code reviews, debugging, and integration testing.

- Document technical designs, test results, and software functionality, and present your completed project to the engineering team.

Required Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

- Demonstrated software development experience through personal projects, engineering teams, research, open-source contributions, or previous internships.

- Experience programming in at least one language such as C, C++, Rust, or Python.

- Strong understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts, including debugging, testing, data structures, and software design.

- Familiarity with collaborative development tools and practices such as Git, code reviews, or automated testing.

- Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and the ability to independently work through unfamiliar technical challenges.

- Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and collaborate effectively with engineers across disciplines.

Desired Qualifications

- Experience developing software that interacts with physical hardware, embedded systems, or robotics platforms.

- Familiarity with Linux development environments and command-line tooling.

- Experience developing test automation, simulation software, or continuous integration pipelines.

- Familiarity with networking concepts and communication protocols such as TCP/IP, UDP, Ethernet, CAN, UART, or SPI.

- Experience with embedded Linux, device drivers, or low-level systems programming.

- Hands-on experience with spacecraft, rocketry, CubeSats, robotics, Formula SAE, autonomous vehicles, or similar engineering projects.

Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in office presence for the duration of the internship.

The California annual base hourly rate for this role is currently $38-$41. Pay Grades are determined by role, level, location, and alignment with market data.  Individual pay will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: interviews and an assessment of several factors that are unique to each candidate, job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and internal equity.
ITAR Compliance:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR  here .

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Inversion provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

rows.title: Software Engineer, AI Platform - New Grad
rows.description:
Who We Are

Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.

Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.

With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.

Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.

About the Role

Our software team is growing, and we are looking for talented engineers who are graduating by December 2026 to join us and be instrumental to one of the following areas: Data Platform, Onboard Systems, ML Infrastructure, Simulation, or Technical Infrastructure teams.

About the Work

Depending on your skill set and areas of interest you will work on some or all of the following:

- Data Platform: The Data Platform serves as a comprehensive management system for Nuro AI Driver's data, labels, and metrics, facilitating seamless access functionality. The team focuses on data annotation across various domains, including 2D/3D perception, mapping, behavior trajectory, and language/text. It also handles data ingestion and mining, employing methods such as heuristics and embedding search. Additionally, the platform supports the autonomy evaluation infrastructure by providing detailed introspection.

- Onboard Systems: Our onboard system team’s software engineers provide a reliable and high-performance platform that allows our autonomy teams to integrate their autonomy software and algorithms that work across various self-driving platforms. This work requires close collaboration with our software teams, hardware teams, and systems/safety team to make sure new software and hardware work together safely and reliably and resolve onboard error and performance problems.

- Technical Infrastructure: this group owns few fundamental services for entire engineering organizations: generic compute platform to host mission-critical workflows such as data processing and simulation, storage management service which manages hundreds of PB of data, cloud infrastructure serves as IaaC which provisions and maintains all cloud resources, engineering productivity provides tools such as build and CI/CD to make engineering work more efficient.

About You

You have deep expertise and prior experience in some or many of the following areas:

- You are a current Bachelor’s Degree or Master’s Degree candidate in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or related field, graduating before or in June 2027.

- You have experience in one or more of the following areas: large-scale distributed systems; data storage and processing systems; advanced algorithms using C++ and Python; machine learning, multithreading; x86 architecture; and software performance tuning and optimization, robotics software frameworks, different compute modalities (CPU, GPU, FPGA) etc.

- You have strong problem-solving and programming skills.

At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $153,000 to $176,000 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package

At Nuro, we celebrate differences and are committed to a diverse workplace that fosters inclusion and psychological safety for all employees. Nuro is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and expressly prohibits any form of workplace discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

rows.title: Software Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
rows.description:
Sigma unlocks the value of data by delivering cloud-scale analytics and business intelligence with the simplicity of a spreadsheet, complete with pivot tables and dashboards. We empower business professionals and data teams to quickly explore, analyze, visualize, and collaborate, leveraging all of their data across the organization.

Our internship program at Sigma:

Sigma’s Early Career Program is the launchpad for the next generation of engineers and innovators. As an Intern at Sigma, you’ll work on various production features and learn efficient engineering for large scalable systems. Our interns work directly with our engineers, product leaders, and designers across the organization everyday. We’re looking for students who bring curiosity, a spirit for collaboration, and a desire for shaping the future of business insights and data exploration.

Internship Program Qualifications:

- Current student :

- Applicants must be currently enrolled in a university undergraduate or graduate degree program in the U.S with a graduation date of December 2027 or later

- Able to intern from June 2027 through August/early September 2027 (dates flexible)

- Authorization :

- You must be legally authorized to work in the US during the Summer 2027 program

- Visa sponsorship is not available for our internship positions

- Location:

- Our remaining internships are in-person and located primarily within San Francisco, CA or New York, NY. Relocation assistance will be provided for students who will need to relocate for the Summer in the form of a relocation bonus.

- Applicants must be able to work in-person in our office in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY for the duration of their internship

About the role:

Sigma’s Engineering organization is a dynamic, high performing team of Software Engineers who complement each other's skills. Our Engineers design, implement, and scale technical solutions that power our core product and enable our users to make data driven decisions in their businesses. As a Software Engineering Intern , you will experiment, prototype, and implement features that help our global user base analyze and gather insights from their data. During your internship, you’ll partner directly with your engineering mentor, as well as collaborate with other teams across the business. From Product Designers, Product Managers, Sales, and, of course, actual users, you will collaborate across the company to determine the best solution for your technical challenge. Interns will take their project from ideation through implementation, iterating and gathering feedback along the way. As an intern, you will deploy features and gather insights from customer metrics to aid you in making better development decisions and improve your business acumen.

During your internship you will:

- Learn how to build production software and understand how large Single Page Applications are built and extended with the user experience top of mind

- Experience how backend scales to handle multiple customers and billions of data points while keeping user information secure

- Gain an understanding of how to own a development project from beginning to end

- Develop automated unit tests to get the relevant code coverage and work with product owners and techpubs to document your work

- Partner with other Engineers, Product Managers, and Designers

- Design and deliver innovative solutions to improve the Sigma user experience by implementing new features into our product

- Find new ways to optimize the performance of one or more components of the product

What we’re looking for:

- Applicants must be pursuing at least a Bachelor’s or a Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field

- Have an intermediate to advanced grasp of Operating Systems, Data structures, algorithms and at least one modern programming language such as Java, Python, JavaScript, etc.

- Excited to learn and build complex user interfaces, data visualizations, or backend systems

- Solid project management and communication abilities. You love to find the right resources and can own tasks end to end with minimal supervision.

- Have a drive and desire to navigate unknowns, after all, that’s what unlocks realizations

- Ability to collaborate and work in a team environment

- Able to commit 40 hrs a week for 12 weeks in-person in our San Francisco, CA or New York, NY office

- Ready to start work full-time by either January 2028 or June 2028 (preferred)

Additional Job details

Interns at Sigma are compensated with an hourly rate and relocation bonus (where applicable). Our hourly rate for this role is $50.00 per hour.

rows.title: Senior Software Engineer I/II, Back-end/Data, Robotics
rows.description:
Your Impact at LILA

You will build the back-end and data foundations of the systems that schedule work across our autonomous labs, model them as digital twins, and turn raw experimental output into trustworthy, queryable data. In Robotics, you'll own core services scientists, operators, and engineers rely on daily — the ones that decide how efficiently our robots run and how much our scientists trust their data.

What You'll Be Building

- Design scheduling systems: allocate experiments, instruments, and compute across autonomous labs, modeling long-running jobs as durable Temporal workflows.

- Model digital twins: stand up the simulation/digital-twin data layer so teams predict factory behavior before committing resources.

- Own technical data management: build the Flyte pipelines, S3 lakehouse, and PostgreSQL models that turn instrument output into governed, trustworthy data.

- Enable data science: ship batch and event-driven pipelines that put clean data in the hands of scientists and models.

- Deliver capacity planning: create customer-facing services that help teams forecast factory capacity.

- Operate for scale: run services on AWS EKS with Docker/ECR, Terraform, and GitHub Actions, reliable as the factory grows.

What You'll Need to Succeed

- 4–8 years of back-end engineering: production services in Python (FastAPI) at scale.

- Data engineering: pipelines on a workflow orchestrator such as Flyte, Temporal, or similar.

- Data modeling across stores: hands-on SQL (PostgreSQL), object storage (S3), and data lakehouse architectures.

- Cloud-native delivery: a major cloud with containers, infrastructure as code, and CI/CD — ideally AWS EKS (Docker/ECR), Terraform, and GitHub Actions.

- End-to-end ownership: taking services from design through delivery, reliability, and iteration.

- Clear collaboration: communicating technical tradeoffs plainly with engineers, scientists, and business partners.

Bonus Points For

- Systems engineering in regulated industries: systems-thinking rigor in safety- or quality-critical settings — aerospace, manufacturing, or healthcare/life sciences. Exposure to 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+, GAMP 5 / FDA CSA, or ISA-95 a plus.

- Domain exposure: robotics, lab automation, LIMS, or manufacturing/MES environments.

- Scheduling & optimization: job scheduling, resource allocation, or constraint/optimization problems.

- Data-science enablement: distributed compute (Ray), experiment tracking (Weights & Biases), or model serving.

- Event-driven messaging: NATS, MQTT, or similar pub/sub for high-volume telemetry.

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. rows.title: Cloud Platform Engineer - New Grad
rows.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Team

The Cloud Platform team runs the production inference service that serves SambaNova's models to customers on RDU accelerators. We handle deployment, monitoring, capacity planning, and incident response across regions in the United States, Asia, Europe, and Latin America.

About the Role

As a new grad Cloud Platform Engineer, you'll write automation and infrastructure code that keeps our inference service fast and available. You'll build monitoring and dashboards, manage Kubernetes clusters and Terraform modules, help stand up new regions, and join a shared on-call rotation once you're ramped up.

- Operate and maintain Kubernetes clusters that run our inference workloads

rows.title: Software Engineer Intern, Inference
rows.description:
At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.


THE ROLE

Our foundation world models have to run fast enough to control robots in the real world, and efficiently enough to support large-scale research. As an Inference Infrastructure Engineer Intern, you'll work with our infra and research engineers to make model inference faster and more efficient across the stack, from data pipelines down to GPU kernels. You'll own a scoped, high-impact project end to end, ship it into our production or research workflow, and present your results to the team.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Profile and benchmark inference for large video and world models to find bottlenecks in latency, throughput, and memory.

 - Apply and evaluate inference optimization techniques like quantization and low-precision inference, step distillation and sampling acceleration for diffusion-style models, attention and caching optimizations across frames, model compilation, and graph-level optimizations.

 - Make data movement and processing more efficient: video decoding and preprocessing, input pipelines, host–device transfer, caching, and storage/IO paths that feed inference and training.

 - Write and tune GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, or similar) for performance-critical operators, and integrate them into our inference stack.

 - Build tooling and benchmarks that let the team track performance regressions and improvements reliably.

 - Work with researchers to turn promising ideas into production-quality infrastructure.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You don't need all of these. Strong depth in any one of the areas below is enough to apply:

 - ML inference optimization: hands-on experience making deep learning models run faster or cheaper, e.g. quantization (INT8/FP8), pruning/distillation, operator fusion, mixed precision, or compilers and runtimes such as torch.compile, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, or TVM.

 - Data efficiency optimization: experience speeding up data loading and preprocessing pipelines (especially video or other high-bandwidth sensor data), cutting IO and memory overhead, or improving data/compute utilization in ML systems.

 - GPU kernel optimization: experience writing or tuning GPU kernels in CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar; familiarity with the GPU memory hierarchy, occupancy, and profiling tools (Nsight Systems/Compute, PyTorch profiler).


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

 - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field.

 - Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++.

 - Solid understanding of deep learning fundamentals and at least one framework (PyTorch preferred).

 - Comfortable reading performance data and reasoning about trade-offs between latency, throughput, memory, and accuracy.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with video model inference is a huge plus, e.g. optimizing video generation, video diffusion, or world models, or real-time video understanding pipelines.

 - Research experience in systems or ML, e.g. publications or substantial research projects (MLSys, OSDI/SOSP, CVPR/ICCV, NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR, or similar).

 - Experience with real-time or latency-critical inference, e.g. on robots or edge/embedded accelerators.

 - Experience with multi-GPU inference (tensor/sequence/pipeline parallelism).

 - Contributions to open-source ML systems projects.


WHAT YOU'LL GET

 - A real project with measurable impact on robots operating in the real world.

 - Mentorship from experienced infra and research engineers.

 - Access to modern GPU compute for experiments.

rows.title: Inference Engineering, Co-op
rows.description:
Overview

Inferact's mission is to grow vLLM as the world's AI inference engine and accelerate AI progress by making inference cheaper and faster. Founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, we sit at the intersection of models and hardware, a position that took years to build.

 

About the Role

We're looking for exceptional University of Waterloo co-op students who want to work on the systems that determine how fast, efficiently, and reliably frontier AI models run on frontier workloads at scale. This is not a sandboxed internship project. We will match your strengths and interests to a real engineering problem across the vLLM stack, from model execution and low-level accelerator code to distributed serving and the cloud platform that makes it all usable.

You'll work alongside the creators and core maintainers of vLLM on work intended to ship into open source, production systems, or the tooling that supports both. You will have a primary technical track, meaningful ownership, and mentorship from a small, senior team, with opportunities to collaborate across models, compilers, accelerators, networking, and distributed systems. The goal is to let exceptional students learn at the frontier while making contributions used by developers and AI teams around the world.

 

Potential Focus Areas

Your co-op will have a primary home in one of the following tracks, with opportunities to contribute across others:

 - Inference Runtime: Bring new model architectures and inference techniques to life in vLLM. Implement ideas from research papers; support mixture-of-experts, multimodal, diffusion, and agentic workloads; and improve scheduling, continuous batching, KV-cache memory management, prefix caching, and hybrid model serving.

 - Performance & Scale: Build the distributed serving data plane that lets vLLM run across many GPUs and nodes. Work on tensor, expert, or context parallelism; prefill/decode separation and KV-cache transport; fault tolerance and multi-tenancy; and high-performance communication using NCCL, DeepEP, NVSHMEM, RDMA, or InfiniBand.

 - Kernel Engineering: Raise the hardware performance ceiling by writing and optimizing attention, GEMM, sampling, KV-cache, fused, and quantization kernels. Use CUDA, Triton, TileLang, CUTLASS/CUTE, or related tools; reason about memory hierarchy, occupancy, and tensor cores; and prove speedups through profiling, correctness tests, and reproducible benchmarks.

 - AMD GPU Performance: Help make vLLM first-class on AMD accelerators. Work across ROCm, HIP, Triton, CK, AITER, kernels, runtime paths, quantization, compiler integration, and performance-regression infrastructure while learning how AMD-specific execution, memory, and toolchain constraints shape inference.

 - TPU Performance: Help make vLLM fast and correct on Google TPUs. Build backend, runtime, and compiler integrations with JAX, XLA, Pallas, MLIR, and related tooling; inspect compiler artifacts; work on lowering, fusion, and code generation; and benchmark production-relevant serving across correctness, latency, and throughput.

 - Cloud Orchestration: Build the operational platform that makes large-scale inference deployable and reliable. Work on Kubernetes and custom operators, topology-aware GPU scheduling, zero-downtime vLLM rollouts, token-aware routing, observability, infrastructure-as-code, automated recovery, and bring-your-own-cloud or multi-cloud fleet management.

You are not expected to arrive with experience in every track. We care most about unusual depth or learning velocity in one area, strong fundamentals, and evidence that you can turn a difficult problem into working, measurable software.

 

Skills and Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

 - Currently pursuing a bachelor's, master's, or PhD degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, or a related technical field, and eligible for a University of Waterloo co-op work term.

 - Strong programming ability in Python, C++, Rust, Go, or another systems-oriented language.

 - Strong computer science fundamentals and the ability to learn from research papers, technical documentation, and complex systems code.

 - Evidence that you have built and debugged nontrivial software through coursework, research, a prior internship, open-source work, or an ambitious side project.

 - A builder mindset: you define what success means, measure results, validate correctness, communicate clearly, and keep iterating until the system works.

Preferred qualifications:

 - Depth in at least one relevant area such as ML or inference systems, distributed systems, GPU or accelerator programming, compilers, high-performance computing, operating systems, networking, Kubernetes, or cloud infrastructure.

 - Hands-on experience with one or more relevant technologies such as PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, CUDA, Triton, TileLang, ROCm/HIP, JAX/XLA, Pallas, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Ray, or SLURM.

 - Experience profiling or benchmarking software, validating numerical or systems correctness, or building tests that protect against performance regressions.

 - Experience with systems beyond a single local process or device, including multi-GPU, multi-node, research-cluster, high-throughput, or production-like workloads.

Bonus points if you have:

 - Contributed to open-source ML, systems, compiler, or infrastructure projects, especially vLLM or adjacent projects.

 - Built a research system, benchmark suite, compiler or kernel project, distributed service, or infrastructure tool that demonstrates unusual technical depth and initiative.

 - Worked across more than one layer of the stack and enjoy moving between algorithms, runtimes, systems, and hardware rather than staying inside a single abstraction.

 - Created a technical artifact such as a paper, design document, blog post, demo, or talk that clearly explains what you built and what you learned.

 

Meet Inferact at Waterloo

Interested in learning more about Infe

In this role, you will combine hands-on cell culture with laboratory automation to deliver consistent, high-quality materials for downstream applications. Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings.

Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025.

rows.title: Senior Software Engineer, Internal Tools
rows.description:
ABOUT US


Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.

We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future.

About You 

We're a small, high output team, mostly former founders including YC alumni, and we operate with real autonomy and almost no bureaucracy. We hire on competence, not pedigree. Leaders are in the office six days a week, and we generally expect the team to be available six days a week too. Not because we count hours, but because there's always more wood to chop when revolutionizing how tomorrow’s healthcare providers deliver care to their patients today. We trust our team to take the time off they need and we've never said no to a time off request.

You have an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong sense of ownership. You don't wait to be told what's broken. Instead, you believe you can figure out any problem that lands in your lap even outside your exact domain. When someone scopes something for three weeks, you ask why it can't be done in three days, and you also know the difference between shipping a fast v0 and cutting a corner that comes back to bite you. You walk the tightrope between craft and speed without falling off either side.




THE ROLE

You're obsessed with automating repetitive tasks, your first instinct when you see a manual process is "how do I make this run by itself?" At Metriport, you'll own the internal tooling that keeps our company moving fast. You'll spot the friction, build the fix, and ship it  without waiting to be asked.

 - You're entrepreneurial minded, with the drive to push work forward even when it's not anyone else's top priority.

 - You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable working directly with stakeholders across Eng, Ops, and business teams to understand their needs and translate them into working solutions.

 - You're a hacker at heart, you get excited about wiring together services that weren't built to talk to each other, and you know how to make it work securely and at scale.

 - You keep security top of mind. We work with sensitive healthcare data, and you treat that seriously, vetting third party integrations, applying least privilege thinking, and never cutting corners that could expose PHI.

 - You follow the AI tooling space closely and try to use it to solve real business problems, but you have the judgment to know what's appropriate for an enterprise context and what's a hard no.

 - You care about outcomes over elegance. A Slack bot that saves the Ops team an hour a day is worth more than a perfect abstraction nobody uses.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

After ramping up on our internal tools and workflows, you'll own the systems that make our teams more efficient and more secure. Day to day, this looks like:

 - Automating cross functional processes: many of our internal processes are still manual and error prone; you'll work with non engineering functions at Metriport to automate away their friction within the company

 - Building Automations End to End: Designing and shipping integrations between our internal and third party systems from scoping the requirement with a stakeholder, to deploying a working solution, to making sure it doesn't break quietly.

 - Improving Developer Experience and Onboarding: Automating local environment setup for new engineers, improving CICD speed, reducing the time to production from hours to minutes.

 - Evaluating and Adopting New Tools: Researching integration platforms (Zapier, n8n, Make, etc.) and AI productivity tools, working with the Security team to assess their security posture, and rolling them out in a way that meets our compliance requirements.

 - Reporting: Automating recurring reports by pulling from AWS Athena, REST APIs, and other data sources so the team gets accurate data without manual effort every month.

 - Team alignment: Participating in a daily 30 minute remote standup at 7:30 AM PST Mon–Fri (our only regular mandatory meeting).




REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of experience in a software engineering, automation, or internal tools role ideally at a startup where you wore multiple hats.

 - TypeScript proficiency: Our entire stack is TypeScript. You write clean, maintainable TS without hand holding.

 - React proficiency: Our internal operations tool is React based. You can build and extend UI components to surface new workflows.

rows.description:
Who we are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across AI, hardware, software, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are researchers, roboticists, engineers, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About the role

We are seeking an AI Research Intern to join our founding team and bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. In this role, you will contribute to core research initiatives on Perception, World Models and Action models. You will help translate cutting-edge theoretical breakthroughs into scalable, real-world deployment on physical autonomous systems, driving how our platforms perceive, simulate, and navigate complex environments.

What you’ll do

- Integrate and adapt emerging AI research into internal model pipelines, validating performance on real-world datasets and simulation.

- Prototype and evaluate RL, trajectory planning, and distillation algorithms based on state-of-the-art literature.

- Train and fine-tune multimodal models that map real-time sensor inputs and behavioral goals to vehicle actuation.

- Experiment with world model architectures using multi-sensor log data to improve simulation fidelity and trajectory querying.

- Analyze edge cases and failure modes in novel driving environments to iterate on model performance and stability.

- Run rigorous simulation experiments alongside research and validation teams to identify performance bottlenecks and track model improvements.

What we're looking for

- Education: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, EECS, Robotics, AI, or a closely related field.

- Core Expertise: Coursework, project experience, or research background focused on at least one of the following domains:

- Generative World Models / Video Generation / Diffusion Models

- Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or embodied AI

- Reinforcement Learning (RL), trajectory optimization, or decision-making systems

- Large-scale multimodal Transformer architectures applied to robotics or spatio-temporal data

- Framework Fluency: Advanced hands-on proficiency with PyTorch or JAX for training and fine-tuning large-scale neural networks.

- Programming: Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of C++.

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior research, project, or internship experience in autonomous driving, mobile robotics, or spatial AI.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our Mountain View or San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change, we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

The hourly pay range for this internship role is $70/hr per hour.

Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Atoms accepts applications on an ongoing basis.

Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?
