rows.title: Senior Director, Mining Autonomous Platform (AV Platform Engineering)
rows.description:
Who we are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About the role

We are hiring a Senior Director, Mining Autonomy Platform Engineering to lead the team that owns the platform beneath our autonomous mining products.

What you’ll do

- Retrofit and integration architecture. Own the architecture of the autonomy installation across supported trucks, including electrical architecture, harness design, mounting, sensor and compute placement, and power. Define what is common across trucks and what is configured per model, and maintain a documented integration path for a new truck type.

- Bring-up and commissioning engineering. Own the build instructions, drawings, procedures, and commissioning gates that installations run against. Act as the engineering escalation point for field teams and convert escalations into documented design and process changes.

- Off-machine validation. Build and own the bench and simulation capability that allows releases to be validated against real truck interfaces. Own the correlation between bench behavior and truck behavior, including where the two diverge.

- Reliability, diagnostics, and fleet measurement. Own availability, utilization, and subsystem failure-rate measurement, including fault attribution. Set diagnostics requirements for new hardware, and run root-cause and corrective-action discipline on field failures.

- Configuration control. Own per-truck configuration integrity, including validation at commissioning that installed hardware matches what the software expects.

- Team building. Hire and lead the mining platform engineering team. Set the technical bar and develop engineers who can handle routine bring-ups independently.

- Engineering standards. Establish and enforce conventions for schematics, circuit naming, labeling, harness documentation, and change control across internal teams and suppliers. Lead design reviews, DFMEA, and structured root-cause processes.

What we’re looking for

- Required: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field with 12+ years of relevant experience, or a master's with 10+.

- Experience leading engineers on an autonomous or similar program, including hiring, setting technical direction, and delivering against committed dates.

- Ownership of a vehicle or machine integration platform from architecture through field deployment, with personal accountability for how the system was installed, validated, and supported.

- Hands-on experience with machine and vehicle networks (CAN, CAN FD, automotive Ethernet); drive-by-wire and actuation integration; electrical and harness architecture for harsh environments; embedded compute and sensor integration; hardware-in-the-loop and bench validation.

- Experience converting bespoke, per-customer or per-platform engineering into a configurable product with documented interfaces.

- Working understanding of autonomous systems end to end, including sensing, perception, localization, planning, controls, and the associated safety architecture.

- Track record of establishing reliability, availability, or failure-rate measurement that changed how an organization set priorities.

- Experience acting as the senior technical presence at a customer or partner site during a launch or a failure.

- Strong written practice covering architecture documents, integration specifications, and failure analyses.

- Willingness to travel regularly to active mine and quarry sites, domestic and international. Site work requires PPE, lifting up to 50 lbs, and working at rack level, on machines, and in operating pits, with or without reasonable accommodation.

- Ability to work onsite five days a week in San Francisco.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

What else you need to know

This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.

rows.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Backend
rows.description:
The Team + The Role

The Core team builds features and platform capabilities that power critical areas of the Pendo product experience. Our work supports high-stakes customer use cases, drives how our systems evolve, and creates a consistent experience across the platform. We operate in complex product areas where delivery speed, system reliability, and long-term maintainability are equally important.

As a Sr. Software Engineer, you own complex technical challenges and drive solutions independently. You apply sound engineering judgment, partner with product and design, and take accountability for outcomes, not just output. You break ambiguous work into small, continuously shippable increments, bring others along, and improve the codebase as you deliver.

This role is based in our Raleigh office.

What this looks like day-to-day

- End-to-end feature ownership: Own complex, ambiguous features from problem definition through delivery. Break work into small, independently shippable increments to maintain consistent progress and deliver customer value.

- Production-quality engineering: Write reliable, maintainable production code and select testing approaches based on risk and system impact. Apply safe rollout patterns, including feature flags and incremental deployments, to reduce delivery risk.

- Production reliability: Respond quickly to production issues within your area of ownership and drive them to resolution. Identify root causes and implement improvements that prevent recurring problems.

- AI-enabled development: Integrate AI tools into daily engineering workflows for code generation, debugging, test writing, and task decomposition. Share effective practices that improve how the team uses AI to build and deliver software.

- Technical collaboration: Provide actionable code reviews and contribute constructively to engineering discussions and planning. Partner with product, design, and fellow engineers to align technical decisions with product outcomes.

- Continuous improvement: Identify recurring friction in code, tests, tooling, and development processes. Proactively implement improvements that strengthen engineering quality and team efficiency.

- Clear technical communication: Create documentation, commit messages, and technical notes that make decisions and implementation details easy to understand. Maintain enough written context for teammates to continue work without requiring verbal handoffs.

Who You Are

Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work.

You're a builder, not a maintainer.

You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Sr. Software Engineers don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work.

You're AI-curious - genuinely.

You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut.

Must-haves

- 5+ years of software engineering experience delivering customer-facing SaaS product features in production environments.

- Strong proficiency in at least one backend programming language: Go, Java, Python, or C++.

- Deep understanding of scalable web architecture, API design, and performance optimization.

- Experience with AWS or GCP cloud platforms and both SQL and NoSQL databases.

- Demonstrated ability to independently structure ambiguous technical work into small, deliverable increments and drive execution through completion.

- Experience designing and implementing unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, with sound judgment about when to apply each approach.

- Familiarity with safe deployment and rollout practices, including feature flags, canary releases, or comparable approaches.

- Active use of AI tools in software development workflows.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, product, and design teams.

- Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience improving team-level engineering tooling, development processes, or developer workflows beyond individual feature delivery.

- Experience mentoring engineers and strengthening team capabilities through technical documentation, constructive code reviews, or knowledge sharing.

- Experience contributing to shared platform capabilities that support multiple product areas.

About Pendo

Pendo was founded in 2013 by former product managers, who combined their heads and hearts to build something they wanted but never had as product managers: a simple way to understand and attack what truly drives product success. Our mission is to improve society's experience with software. Come join one of the fastest-growing startups, supported by best-in-class institutions like Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Spark Capital and Meritech.

Pendo Core Values: Bias to Act, Hone Your Craft, The Team is Pendo, and Maniacal Focus.

Location: Pendo is a hybrid culture. In-office 3 days per week unless designated remote.

Compensation: The expected salary range for this role to be performed in Raleigh, NC is $135,000 - $150,000.

Benefits: Highly competitive, employer-heavy coverage (including $0 premium options), strong 401(k) match, equity, and flexible time off.

EEOC: We are an equal opportunity employer and believe having diverse teams where everyone brings their whole self to Pendo is key to our success. We welcome all people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities
